title: Inference Observability Synthesis — Release Working Group
body:
Purpose
This doc captures the working-group decisions and concrete instrumention guidance for the upcoming inference release. Focus is on bridging traces to metrics, standardizing dashboard layouts for token-serving paths, and introducing cost-aware alert heuristics. It is a synthesis: pragmatic rules the release team can apply immediately and a migration plan for older dashboards.

Goals
- Clear, unambiguous metric definitions for service-level and model-level telemetry.
- Deterministic mapping from trace spans to aggregated metrics used in SLOs.
- Dashboards that surface regressions in latency, correctness, and cost per 1K tokens.
- Alerting that prioritizes user impact and cost spikes, with low false-positive rate.
- Lightweight migration path for legacy panels (keep-while-coexist strategy).

Audience
Primary: serving runtime engineers, SREs, product owners for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Secondary: solutions engineers and customer support who rely on dashboards for incident context.

Metric definitions (canonical)
- request_count: counter, labels={route, model, region, client_tier, status_code_family}, description="Total inference requests received by gateway". Increment on request accept.
- token_generated_total: counter, labels={model, route, region, quantization_profile}, description="Total tokens generated (output) by renderer". Emit from renderer on chunk flush.
- input_token_total: counter, labels={model, route, region}, description="Total tokens consumed (input) for requests".
- latency_p50_p95_p99_ms: histograms/buckets, labels={model, route, region, phase}, description="Client-visible latency broken out by phase (gateway, routing, execution)". Use consistent buckets: [1,2,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2000].
- kvcache_hit_ratio: gauge (derived), labels={model, route}, description="(cached_prefix_tokens)/(lookup_attempts) over rolling 5m". Export as numerator/denominator to avoid NaN.
- batching_size_p50_p95: histogram, labels={instance_pool, model}, description="Batch sizes observed in runtime batching queue".
- gpu_utilization_pct: gauge, labels={host, gpu_type, instance_pool}, description="GPU utilization averaged over 1m".
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: derived gauge, labels={model, quantization_profile, route}, description="Estimated USD per 1000 tokens using current pricing model and utilization amortization".
- error_rate_4xx_5xx: counter, labels={model, route, error_code}, description="HTTP level error counts".

Tracing & span design guidance
- Top-level trace root: request root span at gateway with trace_id and these tags: route, model, client_id, region, request_id. Root must attach sampling decision and a provenance tag (hosted|dedicated|private).
- Standardized child spans: routing (time taken in policy evaluation), queue (time in batching queue), execution (model forward), kv-cache-lookup, kernel-exec (if measurable), response-streaming.
- Each execution span must emit attributes: seq_len_in, seq_len_out, kvcache_warmed, batch_size, quantization_profile, host_id.
- Span status mapping: span.status=OK/ERROR; add attribute error_type for categorization.
- Low-overhead sampling policy: deterministic sampling tiers based on client_tier and error presence: 100% traces for errors and latency > p99, 5% for production free-tier, 20% for enterprise routes. Deterministic sampling ensures stable tail latency investigations.

Trace-to-metric mapping rules
- Request_count comes from root span accept events. Signal derived when root span is created.
- Token counters emitted from execution span when chunk flush event occurs; execution span must write a marker event with tokens_out and tokens_in to assist 로그 reassembly.
- Latency histograms populated using root span duration (client-visible), with optional phase-tagged histograms taken from child spans. This supports heatmap slicing by phase.
- kvcache_hit_ratio: instrumentation emits kvcache_hit and kvcache_miss counters at kv-cache-lookup span boundaries. Use PromQL rate(kvcache_hit[5m]) / rate(kvcache_lookup[5m]).

Dashboard layout guidance (single pane to serve multiple personas)
- Top row: health summary (request_count 1m, error_rate_4xx_5xx 1m, top-3 alert states, global cost_per_1k_tokens_usd).
- Second row: latency summary by model and route (p50/p95/p99) with phase drill-down toggles.
- Third row: resource & batching (gpu_utilization_pct, batching_size_p95, queue_length heatmap).
- Fourth row: correctness / quality signals (sparklines of model evaluation metrics from eval pipeline, if available), fallback activations count.
- Right sidebar: sampling trace links for p99 errors (linking to trace UI with pre-filtered query).
- Panel conventions: always include model and route filters at top, time-range persistent +/- 6h/24h/7d. Panels should avoid high-cardinality label expansion by default (use top-k).

Queries examples (PromQL-like pseudocode)
- request_rps: sum(rate(request_count{route=~".*"}[1m])) by (route, model)
- p95_exec_latency_ms: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(latency_bucket{phase="execution"}[5m])) by (le, model))
- kvcache_hit_rate: sum(rate(kvcache_hit[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(kvcache_lookup[5m])) by (model)
- cost_spike_detector: increase(cost_estimate_usd[15m]) > scalar(0.5) AND increase(request_cost_estimate[15m]) / increase(request_count[15m]) > scalar(0.03)

Alerting principles and example alerts
- Principle: prioritize user-impacting regressions first (latency/error SLO breaches), then cost regressions that are sustained and actionable.
- Alert: model-high-latency-p99 — when p99 latency for a model exceeds 2x target for 15m and request_rate > 5rps. Severity: Sev2. Runbook: check recent deploys, trace sampling links, fallback activations.
- Alert: unexpected-5xx-spike — when increase(error_rate_5xx[5m]) > 10x baseline and error_count > 10. Severity: Sev1 if client-facing endpoint.
- Alert: cost-per-1k-spike — if cost_per_1k_tokens_usd increases 30%+ vs rolling 24h baseline for 30m and GPU utilization < 40% (likely misconfiguration). Severity: Sev3 with auto-ticket to finance+infra.

Ownership & SLAs
- Metric emitter ownership: serving-runtime team own request_count, latency histograms, batching_size. Model-onboarding team own model-specific labels and correctness metrics. Observability team owns dashboards, alert definitions, and trace retention policy.
- SLO examples: "Gateway availability" measured as 5xx rate < 0.1% over 30d with 99.95% target. "P99 latency for small request class" target 500ms for hosted-std models.

Migration plan (legacy -> canonical)
- Phase 0 (1 week): audit existing dashboards, tag panels to be deprecated.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): enable dual reporting: legacy metric names + canonical metrics for 2d. Add 'experimental=true' flag to new panels.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): flip default dashboards to canonical, keep legacy dashboards read-only and annotated with sunset date.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): retire legacy panels after 90 days of co-existence unless a stakeholder requests extension.

Operational playbook snippets
- Incident triage quick path: 1) Check health summary; 2) jump to p99 traces for affected model; 3) check recent deploys and model rollouts (Console rollout log); 4) if cost spike, check batch size distribution and model quantization changes.
- Debug recipe for high p99 with low util: check queue_length heatmap (small bursts), check batch_size distribution (too-small batches), check root-cause traces for kernel exec slowdown (attribute kernel_exec_ms).

Open questions for working group
- Do we standardize on a single cost amortization formula across hosted and dedicated (current estimate differs)? Proposal: canonicalize on amortizing instance-hour + GPU-hour + storage by 30-day utilization baseline.
- Do we push kernel-level micro-metrics (kernel_exec_ms per-shader) into main dashboards or keep behind a debug toggle?
- How aggressively should we sample private deployments where trace export might be restricted by customer policy? Draft: require server-side sampling hints and reduced retention.

Next steps and action items
- (Ava) finalize metric proto names and send to runtime owners — due 2025-03-05.
- (Jared) implement kvcache_hit/miss counters in python worker and open PR — due 2025-03-11.
- (Sophie) prototype dashboard in Grafana using new canonical metrics and link to trace queries — due 2025-03-08.
- (Diego) update alert runbooks with explicit trace-links and test paging behavior — due 2025-03-12.

Appendix: lightweight instrumentation checklist (for library authors)
- Provide stable label names: model, route, region, client_tier, quantization_profile.
- Emit counters for successful token flush events with tokens_out and tokens_in.
- Emit batch_size as a histogram rather than gauge.
- Provide an opt-in attribute for "sensitive_payload" when requests include PII so traces are not exported wholesale.
- Backpressure signal: emit queue_backpressure events when queue length > batch_threshold for 3s.

Notes
This doc intentionally blends pragmatic query examples with higher-level policy so teams can adopt parts incrementally. Feedback welcome in the Release WG thread on Confluence or the linked GitHub PR.
